title: AARTO — Organisational Receiving Process Flow
subtitle: Administrative Adjudication of Road Traffic Offences Act 46 of 1998 (as amended by Act 4 of 2019) and the AARTO Regulations, 2026 · As at 19 October 2026

overview.summary: This flow tells an organisation that owns, operates or allows people to drive vehicles what to do, by when, and who hands off to whom, from the moment an AARTO document arrives until the matter closes and lessons feed back into controls. It is built to comply with the law in force today in the proclaimed municipalities, and to be ready for the points demerit system without redesign.

notes.heading: Legal status
notes.text: Proclamation 322 of 2026 (Government Gazette 54917, 29 June 2026) brought sections 17, 18, 19, 19A, 19B, 20, 23 and 29 to 35 of the AARTO Act into operation on 1 July 2026 in the 60 municipalities listed in its Annexure A. Proclamation 323 of 2026 (GG 54918) brought the AARTO Amendment Act 4 of 2019, except section 2(g), into operation in 62 municipalities, adding Johannesburg and Tshwane, where the Act has run since 2008. The AARTO Regulations, 2026 (GG 54922, 30 June 2026, "Regs") give the Act practical effect. The points demerit system (sections 24 to 28) was excluded; the RTIA says the Minister will set its date, and no date has been gazetted. Everywhere else, including the whole Western Cape, the Criminal Procedure Act process continues. Phase 3 (about 151 further municipalities) has not been proclaimed. On 4 August 2026 the RTIA told Parliament it expects Phase 3 in March 2027 (an earlier RTIA annual performance plan had pointed to October–December 2026). Until a proclamation is gazetted, only the 62 municipalities in Annexure A to Proclamation 323 of 2026 follow AARTO. Re-check before adoption and at each 6.6 review.

notes.heading: Live litigation
notes.text: SALGA's urgent application was struck from the roll for lack of urgency on 30 June 2026; its challenge to the funding model may still be heard in the ordinary course. OUTA withdrew its urgent application after the RTIA disclosed that Appeals Tribunal members had been appointed, but continues a review of the 2026 Regulations. Phase 2 remains in force unless a court orders otherwise. The Constitutional Court upheld the Act and the Amendment Act in Organisation Undoing Tax Abuse v Minister of Transport and Others [2023] ZACC 24 (CCT 19/22, 13 July 2023). Status sources checked for v1.1 (15–19 October 2026): acts.co.za commencement notes; rtia.co.za; Bowmans (6 July 2026); SAnews (1 July 2026); JoburgETC (5 August 2026); TopAuto (17 September 2026); Moonstone (6 August 2026).

notes.heading: Labels used throughout
points: ACT = the Act, in force now in the proclaimed municipalities.
REG = the AARTO Regulations, 2026. References marked "verify" could not be read from a text copy of the Gazette and must be checked against the official GPW version.
NC = enacted but not commenced (the demerit system and rehabilitation). Build readiness; do not treat as a current legal duty.
BP = best practice or internal control; not a statutory deadline. Adopt as policy so it becomes binding internally.

notes.heading: Design principle
notes.text: Every AARTO window is short, and a missed nomination window cannot be reopened. The flow therefore runs internal deadlines well inside the statutory ones and counts from actual receipt, not deemed service. Deciding the election by day 14 and lodging by day 21 leaves at least 11 days to correct a rejected or incomplete submission before day 32.

notes.heading: Six interpretation points that shape the flow
points: Counting days and the date of service. The Act does not say business or calendar days. Under the Interpretation Act 33 of 1957 s.4, "days" are calendar days, excluding the first day and including the last, unless the last day is a Sunday or public holiday. "Date of service" is the date the infringer received the document (Act s.1). A posted or electronically served document is deemed served on the tenth day after posting or electronic service, unless evidence to the contrary is adduced (s.30(2)). Because an issuing authority may prove earlier actual receipt, count from the earliest known receipt and treat the deemed date as a backstop only.

Which regime applies. The place of the infringement decides. Infringements in the Annexure A municipalities, Johannesburg and Tshwane follow AARTO; everywhere else, section 341 and 56 notices and summonses under the Criminal Procedure Act continue, and notices issued before commencement are finalised under that Act (s.35(1)). This flow covers AARTO only, but the register must record the issuing authority and municipality for every notice so both streams are managed.

The court election has gone; offences still go to court. The Amendment Act repealed the option to be tried in court at infringement-notice and courtesy-letter stages (s.17(1)(f)(iv) and s.19(2)(b)(iii)). The challenge route is now representation, then appeal or review to the Appeals Tribunal (s.29B), then the Magistrates' Court (s.29I). Separately, where the same facts give rise to an offence and an infringement, the person is dealt with under the Criminal Procedure Act (s.23); offences are recorded on AARTO 32 or notified on AARTO 33 or 33a (Regs reg 2(4)–(7)). Sections 19A(b) and 20(2)(e) still mention court: treat these as drafting residue.

The nomination window. A driver can be nominated only within 32 days of service of the infringement notice, by providing, in the prescribed manner and to the satisfaction of the issuing authority, the driver's name, acceptable identification and residential and postal address (s.17(1)(f)(v), s.17(4)). A courtesy letter offers only representations or payment (s.19(2)(b)). "I was not the driver" is a nomination, not a representation. Missing the window makes the organisation the infringer of record.

The organisation's capacity. An operator under the National Road Traffic Act is served on AARTO 03a (infringements) or 33a (offences); a juristic person that is not an operator is served on AARTO 03 or 33 (Regs reg 2(6)–(7)). Column 9 of Schedule 3 shows whether a charge lies against the driver, the operator or the owner. Operator-liability charges (such as vehicle fitness or loading) stay with the operator, and nominating a driver may not move them: check the charge code before electing. For leased or rented vehicles, the title holder may nominate the organisation as person in control, which starts a new 32-day clock against the organisation; confirm the practice with each lessor.

Demerit points status. Proclamation 322 excluded sections 24 to 28, and Chapter IV applies only to infringements committed after it commences (s.35(2)). However, the SAFLII consolidation records sections 24 to 28 as commenced in Tshwane (1 July 2008) and Johannesburg (1 November 2008). No points have been recorded in practice and the RTIA says the Minister will determine commencement. The Legal Adviser should confirm there is no risk of points being recorded on Johannesburg or Tshwane infringements under the 2026 Schedule 3. Until then, record the Schedule 3 point value of every infringement so exposure is known on day one.

notes.heading: Roles used
notes.text: AARTO Compliance Officer (ACO); Proxy (PRX, registered on eNaTIS for the juristic person); Fleet Manager (FM); HR Manager (HR); Payroll or Finance (FIN); Legal Adviser (LA); Line Manager (LM); Driver (DRV, including contractors and TES workers allowed to drive); Senior Sign-off (SSO, e.g. CFO or COO); Board or Risk / Audit Committee (BOARD).

stages.title: Phase 0 — Readiness (standing obligations)
intro: Phase 0 has no case trigger. It must be complete before the first notice arrives, because the organisation's liability for a notice depends on facts fixed before the infringement: whether it knew who was driving, and whether its service particulars were live (Act s.17(5), s.30).

notes.heading: Driver side of Phase 0
notes.text: Drivers owe nothing under the Act yet, but their later position depends on this phase. If the organisation did not ascertain their particulars before letting them drive, it carries the penalty and fees itself (s.17(5)), whoever was at the wheel.

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: A nomination is only as good as the allocation record behind it. If a pool vehicle's sign-out sheet is blank for the day in question, no later effort will produce a lawful nomination within 32 days.

steps.title: Adopt the policy and procedure
steps.action: Board-approved AARTO policy covering: roles; receipt channels; driver particulars; nomination protocol; who decides the election; cost allocation and lawful recovery; HR consequences; POPIA lawful basis and s.18 notice to drivers; demerit readiness. Cover everyone allowed to drive or control a vehicle: employees, contractors, TES workers, pool-car users, and employees using their own vehicles on business.

steps.action: Before anyone drives or controls a vehicle, ascertain full names, identity document, residential, postal, business and email addresses; keep ID and licence copies, licence code, PrDP category and expiry.

steps.title: Vehicle-to-driver allocation records
steps.action: Logbooks, pool-car sign-out, telematics driver ID, fuel cards and hire agreements must answer "who drove vehicle X at time Y". Camera, operator and unattended-vehicle notices may arrive up to 60 days after the event. A notice may be re-served up to 180 days after the infringement (s.18(1)(b)), and a lessor's nomination starts a new clock. Keep allocation records for at least 12 months after the event, and in all cases until any linked AARTO matter is closed under Phase 5.

steps.title: Contracts and consents
steps.action: Employment and driver agreements: duty to report notices the same day; cooperate with nomination; deal with notices re-issued in own name; notice that demerit checks will be requested (each check requires a signed AARTO 27 under s.33(2); refusal is handled under D3); deduction consent limited to specific debts. Give drivers a POPIA s.18 notice that allocation and telematics data will be used to identify drivers and disclosed to issuing authorities for nomination, and record the lawful basis (s.11(1)(c) legal obligation; s.11(1)(f) legitimate interest).

steps.title: Legacy sweep
steps.action: Query the business registration number and every proxy ID on the AARTO portal and eNaTIS for outstanding notices and enforcement orders, including Johannesburg and Tshwane history. AARTO penalties do not prescribe.

steps.title: Train and raise awareness
steps.action: Train the ACO, proxies, fleet, HR, line managers and drivers, including the same-day forwarding rule and scam awareness: fake AARTO payment websites were reported in September 2026. Pay only through official channels.

stages.title: Phase 1 — Receipt and intake
intro: The clock starts when a document reaches the organisation or its proxy by any service method, not when the ACO first reads it. Day 0 is the day of receipt; the deemed date of service is calculated alongside it.

notes.heading: Driver obligations at this stage
notes.text: Report any notice received personally the same day. Forward electronic notices received on a proxy phone. Do not pay or ignore a notice addressed to the organisation without telling the ACO.

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: Proxy → ACO (same day). Driver → ACO (same day). ACO → LA (offences). ACO → Fleet (allocation data).

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: Electronic service to a proxy's cellphone is valid service on the organisation. If the proxy is on leave or has left, the notice still counts; this is why steps 0.3 and 0.4 matter.

steps.title: Recognise and forward
steps.trigger: Any AARTO document arrives: post, email, SMS or WhatsApp to the organisation or proxy; handed to a driver at the roadside; or placed on a vehicle (AARTO 31).
steps.action: Forward the complete document, all pages and images, to the ACO. A driver who received a roadside notice (AARTO 01 or 02) reports it the same way.
points: Forward the complete document, all pages and images, to the ACO.
A driver who received a roadside notice (AARTO 01 or 02) reports it the same way.

steps.action: Infringement notice (AARTO 01, 02, 03, 03a, 03b) → Phase 2. Courtesy letter (12) → 4.6. Enforcement order (13) → 4.7. Outcome notices (07a/b, 09a–c, 10Aa–d, 15, 36) → Phase 4. Summons notice (33, 33a) or AARTO 32 → 1.5.

steps.title: Validity screen
steps.action: Check: vehicle registered to the organisation on NaTIS at the time (if not, AARTO 08a, verify title and direction); camera notice carries the required image data; AARTO 03, 03a or 03b served within 60 days of the infringement; municipality proclaimed; not a duplicate. Record defects for Phase 2. A suspected defect never stops the clock.

steps.title: Offence screen
steps.trigger: AARTO 32, 33 or 33a received, or the facts disclose an offence arising from the same facts.
steps.action: Escalate to LA the same day. This is a criminal matter under the Criminal Procedure Act (summons, court date, possible conviction), not an administrative election. Identify the driver for the summons.

steps.title: Diarise all clocks
steps.action: Calendar: driver identified by day 3; assessment by day 7; election decided by day 14; lodgement backstop day 21; statutory day 32 from service. Calculate day 32 from both the actual and deemed dates and diarise the earlier.

steps.title: Portal cross-check
steps.action: Check the AARTO portal and eNaTIS for other notices on the same vehicle or registration number, and for any enforcement order already blocking licensing.

stages.title: Phase 2 — Driver identification and assessment
intro: By internal day 7 the organisation must know who was driving, who carries liability for the charge, and whether there are grounds to challenge it. Everything in Phases 3 and 4 depends on the evidence gathered here.

notes.heading: Driver obligations at this stage
notes.text: Give an accurate account of who was driving. Confirm current particulars. Do not give false information: the organisation's sworn nomination relies on it.

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: FM → ACO (allocation data). HR → ACO (particulars). ACO → LA (merits and liability). ACO → HR (referral).

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: Decide the election on evidence, not on who "should" pay. Cost allocation and discipline are separate questions for Phase 5.

steps.title: Identify the driver
steps.action: Match date, time and place to allocation records, telematics, fuel cards and trip authorisations. Record the source relied on.

steps.title: Confirm particulars
steps.action: Confirm the register holds what a nomination needs: full names, acceptable identification, residential and postal address. Attach ID or licence copy. Missing particulars expose the organisation under s.17(5).

steps.action: Tell the driver in writing, give a copy of the notice, and invite their account within 2 working days. A refusal to confirm does not prevent nomination where records prove who was driving.

stages.title: Phase 3 — Election
intro: One option must be exercised, in the prescribed manner, within 32 days of service (s.17(1)(f)). Decide by internal day 14 and lodge by day 21. Once payment or an instalment arrangement is chosen, the matter is concluded and other options are ignored (s.19A(a)), so never lodge a payment and a representation together.

notes.heading: Driver obligations at this stage
notes.text: Cooperate with the nomination and sign any statement asked of them truthfully. Do not pay a notice addressed to the organisation personally without telling the ACO.

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: ACO → commissioner of oaths. ACO or PRX → issuing authority (nomination); ACO → Authority (representations, instalments). FIN → official payment channel.

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: Missing day 32 does more than add a fee. It removes the nomination option for good and leaves the organisation as the infringer of record.

steps.title: Decide the election
steps.action: Choose: nominate; pay at discount; instalments; representation; or AARTO 08a suspect notice. Record reasons. SSO signs off where organisation funds are used.

stages.title: Phase 4 — Outcomes and escalation
intro: Each outcome arrives as a served document with its own clock. Every document goes back through Phase 1 logging before it is acted on.

notes.heading: Driver obligations at this stage
notes.text: Handle any notice re-issued in the driver's own name within 32 days and report the outcome to the ACO.

notes.heading: Hand-offs
notes.text: ACO → LA (Tribunal, revocation). FIN → registering authority or DLTC (enforcement order payment). LA → Tribunal and Magistrates' Court.

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: A rejection notice opens two clocks at once: 32 days to pay and 30 days to appeal. Calendar the shorter one.

steps.title: Nomination successful
steps.action: Confirm the notice against the organisation is cancelled; move the matter to the driver's personal tracker; remind the driver of their own 32 days.

steps.title: Nomination unsuccessful or cancelled
steps.action: If still inside 32 days of the original service, correct and resubmit. If outside, the organisation is liable: pay or make representations at courtesy-letter stage. Record the root cause.

steps.title: Representation allowed
steps.action: Record cancellation. If the representation succeeded because procedure was not followed, watch for re-service within 40 days of finalisation, never later than 180 days after the infringement.

steps.title: Representation rejected
steps.action: Either pay the penalty, representation fee and any courtesy-letter fee, or arrange instalments, within 32 days of service of the notification; or appeal or apply for review to the Tribunal on AARTO 10A within 30 days of receiving reasons, with the fee. The Tribunal clock is shorter: decide by day 20. Late lodgement with the Tribunal needs condonation on good cause (s.29B(3), AARTO 34 (verify use)). Lodging channel: per the RTIA-hosted Appeals Tribunal Rules (LA to confirm).

steps.title: Tribunal process
steps.action: Correct an incomplete appeal (10Aa); attend the hearing (10Ac). On the outcome (10Ad), decide on review or appeal to the Magistrates' Court within 30 days. Late filing in the Magistrates' Court is subject to that court's rules; LA to advise.
points: Correct an incomplete appeal (10Aa); attend the hearing (10Ac).
On the outcome (10Ad), decide on review or appeal to the Magistrates' Court within 30 days.
Late filing in the Magistrates' Court is subject to that court's rules; LA to advise.

steps.title: Courtesy letter
steps.action: Within 32 days: pay the penalty (no discount) plus the courtesy-letter fee, or make representations. Nomination is no longer available. Open a root-cause review.
points: Within 32 days: pay the penalty (no discount) plus the courtesy-letter fee, or make representations.
Nomination is no longer available.
Open a root-cause review.

steps.title: Enforcement order
steps.action: Treat as a priority incident. Until complied with or revoked, no driving licence, PrDP, permit or licence disc may be issued to the infringer or for any vehicle registered in its name; for the organisation, that is the whole fleet. Pay all penalties and fees within 32 days (also possible at a registering authority or DLTC), or apply for revocation on AARTO 14 with proof: payment, a prior instalment arrangement, a prior representation, nomination or appeal, or other substantiated proof. Outcome on AARTO 15.

steps.title: Payment failures
steps.action: Insufficient or dishonoured payment: pay the full amount plus the notice fee within 32 days. Missed instalment: pay the arrears within 7 days.

steps.title: Refund
steps.action: Apply on AARTO 25; outcome on AARTO 25a.

steps.title: Demerit notices (NC)
steps.action: Once Chapter IV commences, record the points against the driver, operator or juristic person and feed the driver track.

stages.title: Phase 5 — Close and records
intro: A matter is closed only when the notice is cancelled, transferred to the driver, or paid with proof, no fees are outstanding, and the portal shows it as clear.

notes.heading: Watch
notes.text: "Paid" is not closed until the portal shows it. Payments through unofficial websites may never reach the Authority.

steps.title: Close
steps.action: Confirm no fees are outstanding and the portal status is clear; record the closure date.
points: Confirm no fees are outstanding and the portal status is clear; record the closure date.

steps.title: Update registers
steps.action: Update the tracker, the driver's infringement history, the vehicle register and the monthly registration-number check.
points: Update the tracker, the driver's infringement history, the vehicle register and the monthly registration-number check.

steps.title: HR outcome
steps.action: Apply the disciplinary code with a fair procedure. Distinguish negligence, repeat infringement, dishonesty (false denial), unauthorised use and failure to report. Apply consistently.
points: Apply the disciplinary code with a fair procedure.
Distinguish negligence, repeat infringement, dishonesty (false denial), unauthorised use and failure to report.
Apply consistently.

steps.title: Cost recovery
steps.trigger: Organisation paid a penalty caused by a driver.
steps.action: Deduct only with the employee's written consent for that specific debt, or as law permits. For loss or damage: fair procedure, a chance to respond, no more than the actual loss, and total deductions no more than 25% of remuneration.
points: Deduct only with the employee's written consent for that specific debt, or as law permits.
For loss or damage: fair procedure, a chance to respond, no more than the actual loss, and total deductions no more than 25% of remuneration.

steps.title: Records retention
steps.action: Keep proof of payment or cancellation while enforcement risk remains, because penalties do not prescribe. Minimise personal information and record reasons for longer retention.
points: Keep proof of payment or cancellation while enforcement risk remains, because penalties do not prescribe.
Minimise personal information and record reasons for longer retention.

steps.title: Monthly reconciliation
steps.action: Query the registration number and all proxy IDs; confirm no new enforcement orders; reconcile the tracker to the portal.
points: Query the registration number and all proxy IDs; confirm no new enforcement orders; reconcile the tracker to the portal.

stages.title: Phase 6 — Governance and learning
intro: Phase 6 turns individual notices into control improvements and board oversight. None of it has a statutory deadline, so it must be fixed in policy or it will be skipped.

steps.title: Exposure dashboard
steps.action: Notices by stage and jurisdiction; timeliness against days 14, 21 and 32; nomination success rate; courtesy letters and enforcement orders; costs; repeat drivers and vehicles; recorded point values.

steps.title: Board reporting
steps.action: Aggregate report: exposure trends, any enforcement order incidents, litigation and regulatory changes, policy changes.

steps.title: Root cause and coaching
steps.trigger: Every courtesy letter or enforcement order; repeat drivers.
steps.action: Treat each as a control failure and identify which Phase 0 or Phase 1 control failed. Coach repeat drivers.

steps.title: Policy and register refresh
steps.trigger: Annually, or on any legal change.
steps.action: Update the policy, registers, proxy list and contact particulars; re-communicate.

steps.title: Training refresh
steps.action: Refresh training for the ACO, proxies, fleet, HR, managers and drivers.

stages.group: Parallel track — driver, licence and demerit readiness
stages.title: Parallel track — driver, licence and demerit readiness
intro: This track follows the person rather than the notice. Its events are triggered by what happens to a driver's licence and personal notices. Items marked NC are readiness steps until Chapter IV commences.

steps.label: D1
steps.title: Licence validity
steps.action: Check licence and PrDP expiry and categories. No one drives on an expired or wrong licence.
points: Check licence and PrDP expiry and categories.
No one drives on an expired or wrong licence.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — driver, licence and demerit readiness

steps.label: D2
steps.title: Personal notice after nomination
steps.action: Track the driver's own notice to closure: an unpaid personal notice leads to an enforcement order that blocks the driver's licence and PrDP renewal, which becomes an operational risk.
points: Track the driver's own notice to closure: an unpaid personal notice leads to an enforcement order that blocks the driver's licence and PrDP renewal, which becomes an operational risk.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — driver, licence and demerit readiness

steps.label: D3
steps.title: Demerit status access
steps.action: Each check requires a signed AARTO 27 for that check or consent period (s.33(2)); a contract clause is notice only, not the prescribed permission. Statement on AARTO 28. If the driver refuses, do not check; consequences only where lawful. Limit use to the stated purpose.

steps.label: D4
steps.title: Point exposure (NC)
steps.action: Rank drivers by recorded points. The threshold is set by regulation under s.29(d); 15 points (6 for learners) is reported; confirm in Regs Chapter 5.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — driver, licence and demerit readiness

steps.label: D5
steps.title: Disqualification (NC)
steps.action: Disqualification follows within 32 days; its length is the excess points × 3 months. Stop driving duties immediately; ensure documents are handed in within 32 days (proof on AARTO 23a); redeploy or start an incapacity process.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — driver, licence and demerit readiness

steps.label: D6
steps.title: Driving while disqualified (NC)
steps.action: Never permit it. It is an offence and adds a further one-year suspension for every instance.

source.section: §10 Parallel track — driver, licence and demerit readiness

steps.label: D7

steps.label: D10
steps.title: Point reduction (NC)
steps.action: One point is removed for every 3 months, unless a court finds deliberate delay. Update the exposure model.

referenceTables.title: Master flow at a glance
intro: Every channel feeds one intake. Phase 3 is the decision point; its outcome either confirms the matter (steps 4.1, 4.3) or escalates it (4.2, 4.4–4.8), and both close in Phase 5. The driver and demerit track is not a phase: it follows the person rather than the notice and runs until the matter closes.

Read each phase column top to bottom to see who acts and who hands off; read each lane left to right to see one party's whole job. The ACO lane is the spine: every other lane connects to it, and the driver track runs underneath from receipt until the person's own matters are closed.

No such proclamation. Phase 3 (about 151 municipalities) had not been gazetted as at 19 October 2026; on 4 August 2026 the RTIA told Parliament it expects Phase 3 in March 2027. Only the 62 municipalities in Annexure A to Proclamation 323 of 2026 follow AARTO.

intro: Sections 19A(b) and 20(2)(e) still refer to electing to be tried in court, although that election was repealed at both notice stages.
Section 20(4) refers to "subsection (3)(a)", which the 2019 amendment omitted.
Section 17(1)(f)(i) and (ii) now overlap: once "major" and "minor" infringements were replaced by "infringement", both give the discounted-payment option.
Section 17(5) joins the required particulars with "or" and ends with a garbled clause ("an infringer, such person is liable"). Read it conjunctively as a matter of policy.
Section 18(7) (32 days to pay) and s.29B(2) (30 days from receipt of reasons to appeal) run from different triggers with different lengths, which is a trap for infringers.
Section 31(2) removes prescription, so penalties can be collected indefinitely, but no retention period is set for infringers' proof of payment.
Section 25(1) says a person is disqualified "within 32 days" after excess points are incurred, leaving unclear whether disqualification starts on or by day 32.

The Tribunal exists, but public information on how to lodge an appeal remains limited. The Regulations should be supported by published Tribunal rules and lodging channels. The RTIA now hosts an "Appeals Tribunal Rules" document (rtia.co.za); LA to confirm its status and the lodging channel.
